sources.title: The two people shaping the future of OpenAI's research
sources.quote_checked: We're both researchers, we pull on technical threads. | When I joined OpenAI in 2017, I was still among the biggest skeptics at the company. | The point when computers can develop new technologies themselves seems like a very important, um, inflection point. | Two years ago the risks that we were imagining were mostly theoretical risks. | It's not really a disagreement, but there is a natural tension between these different objectives.

sources.title: OpenAI is throwing everything into building a fully automated researcher
sources.quote_checked: I think we are getting close to a point where we'll have models capable of working indefinitely | you kind of have a whole research lab in a data center. | a system that you can delegate tasks to that would take a person a few days | I expect Codex to get fundamentally better. | If we really wanted to, we could build an amazing automated mathematician. | I can have it run experiments in a weekend that previously would have taken me like a week to code | If it's so smart and capable, if it can run an entire research program, what if it does something bad? | Until you can really trust the systems, you definitely want to have restrictions in place. | I do feel personal responsibility | Even by 2028, I don't expect that we'll get systems as smart as people in all ways. | The interesting thing is you don't need to be as smart as people in all their ways in order to be very transformative.

sources.title: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki says there is evidence that AI models discover novel insights
sources.quote_checked: I would say it is a form of reasoning, but that doesn't mean it's the same as how humans reason | Reasoning models don't learn how to think in a vacuum, they are rooted in a model that has learned through pre-training | This for me is closest to what I previously emotionally thought of as AGI | I definitely believe we have significant evidence that the models are capable of discovering novel insights

sources.title: In 'An Alien Mind,' OpenAI's Jakub Pachocki Urges Shared Safety Bars
sources.quote_checked: The idea of racing forward at all costs seems absurd once one internalizes the seriousness of the stakes. | Currently I believe that no lab has solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree | I expect and hope for voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established.

sources.title: OpenAI's Chief Scientist Warns No One Is Ready for AI's Next Leap, Calls for 'Extreme Caution'
sources.quote_checked: This is a time that calls for extreme caution. | I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence. | Scaling AI systems has to be constrained by our confidence in safety.
